research_question: Does a constrained lag-aware full-window loss close the MMECG continuous ECG gap for the REM-AlignNet-MTL refinement model, as it did on CR_RVS?
hypothesis: Adding the CR_RVS-proven lag-aware PCC/L1 loss to the MMECG refine model will improve fold-01 full-window (rem_full_ola) PCC above the existing refine baseline 0.420 while preserving Shape-200 morphology near 0.938.
protocol: Fold-01 strict LOSO pilot, WSST input, 30 epochs, no target-subject calibration.
baseline: q1_remalign_mtl_refine_fold01_pilot fold_01 (full-window OLA PCC 0.420, shape-head PCC 0.938; use_lag_aware_loss=false)
changed_variable: Enable constrained lag-aware full-window loss; keep the refine architecture, MMECG data split, WSST input, and all other loss settings fixed to the refine baseline.
controlled_variables: MMECG processed/loso fold_01 strict LOSO split
success_criteria: Training completes for fold_01 and writes checkpoint/config/logs.
Full-window rem_full_ola PCC improves meaningfully above 0.420 (target >=0.55).
Shape-200 head PCC remains near or above 0.87 (baseline 0.938).
If full-window PCC stays near 0.420, keep as pilot and evaluate the wideband arm before scaling.
checkpoint_selection: Use the training script's validation-best checkpoint only; no test-set checkpoint selection.
failure_interpretation: If lag-aware loss does not improve full-window metrics on MMECG (with or without the wideband arm), dense-decoder refinement is insufficient; the next step is explicit cycle assembly from the strong Shape-200 head using predicted anchors/PPI rather than more loss tuning.
